disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.method_warning: Body-gripping traps — including foothold traps, snares, and Conibear-type traps — are generally unlawful for recreational trappers without a special conflict-abatement permit. Cage/live traps are the standard legal method.
license_summary.sealing: Bobcat and river otter pelts must be sealed by WDFW by April 20 of the year following the season; bobcat lower jaw must be turned in at sealing.
license_summary.trapping_license: A Washington trapping license is required to trap furbearers. Check the WDFW page for license types and fees.

verification.confirmation_notes: WDFW trapping regulations page states rules are effective April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027 — the current rule period covering the 2026–27 trapping season. Seasons, county closures, national-forest closures, sealing deadlines, protected-species list, and the recreational body-gripping trap prohibition all read directly from that official page on 2026-09-18.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the WDFW trapping regulations — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false; weasel and Cascade red fox are null because the regulations do not distinguish the species/subspecies by Latin name.
Marten and red fox closure boundaries (four counties; three national forests) are modeled as descriptive special_areas zones — the app cannot resolve exact geographic boundaries.
Detailed trap-placement and hardware rules are not modeled — only the major recreational body-gripping trap prohibition is noted as a warning.
No bag limits are stated on the WDFW trapping page; none are modeled.
